question: In which Indian movement, were the issues faced by indigo planters, first brought to light in 1917?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Champaran Satyagraha.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The issues faced by** indigo planters**, first brought to light in **1917 **in **Champaran Satyagraha**.
 
• Champaran is a district in the state of Bihar, India.
 
• In 1917, the peasants of Champaran were forced to cultivate indigo by the British landlords, which resulted in their exploitation and oppression.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi,** who was then a young lawyer, was invited by a local leader to investigate the matter.
 
• He stayed in Champaran for several months and organized a successful Satyagraha movement against the British landlords.
 
• Here, for the first time in India, Gandhi used Civil Disobedience as tool for satyagraha.
 
• The Tinkathia system was prevalent in Champaran district of Bihar during the British Raj.
 
 
• It was a system of forced cultivation of indigo on a portion of the farmer's land in exchange for rent-free land for personal cultivation.
 
• The farmers of Champaran were compelled to grow indigo on 3/20th of their land (i.e. three kathas per beegha) by the British planters who had leased the land from the local landlords.
